tools.quote: Within the context of the College, staff and students should make use of institutionally approved and secure AI systems. Use of any other AI system requires prior approval from ICT Services, and a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) must be completed in consultation with the Information Compliance Office (ICO).
Where ever possible, make use of institutionally approved and secure AI systems.
Staff should not use unapproved AI systems on their work devices.
In the case where students are required to use a particular GenAI application as part of an assessment task, it is recommended that students are directed towards institutionally approved tools.
tools.anchor: Considerations for Grading in the Context of GenAI

tools.quote: Staff seeking to use public AI Tools must obtain ICT/ICO approval first.
Detectors cannot be used as reliable evidence in a circumstance where the unauthorised use of GenAI is suspected. The College does not support the use of any such tools.
tools.anchor: Considerations Relating to Suspected Breaches of the Academic Integrity Policy

data.quote: Use of AI must be compliant with GDPR principles. This means staff and students cannot input MIC data or the personal data of staff or fellow students into AI systems without written prior consent.
Use of AI must be compliant with GDPR principles. This means staff and students cannot input MIC data or the personal data of staff or fellow students into AI systems without written prior consent.
Fellow students’ assessments, essays, or project work
Internal publications or research outputs not publicly released
Public AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) must not be used with MIC data unless authorisation has been granted and an approved DPIA is in place.
Explicit consent is required before inputting any personal data into an AI system.

While the College would not advise students to input their personal data into an AI system, if a student, independently of College advice, decides to do so, they should be aware and cautious about what personal data they give to AI systems
Students' assignments and data should not be submitted to third party applications without consulting with the College and without obtaining the student’s consent.

safeguards.quote: Those wishing to use AI technology within their work at MIC need to be compliant with the ICT Security Policy and the Information Security Policy.
It is important that you read the terms and conditions of the applications you are using to ensure that you aren't sharing data that you'd rather not share.

legal.quote: Use of AI must be compliant with GDPR principles.

As we move forward and come into compliance with the EU AI Act, we must begin by questioning how we ensure transparency, fairness, lawfulness and individual rights are upheld in our use of AI systems.
A Generative AI's use of data will depend on the terms and conditions set out by the company that owns the application.
